title: Discovery: Embeddings + Rerank for Pioneer Search
summary: Initial discovery to scope embeddings + reranking integration. Customer currently on hybrid vector store + keyword search, evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployment for throughput, dimensionality tradeoffs, and rerank step. Key asks: support for HNSW/ANN, batching throughput, 1536 vs 768 dims, privacy/KMS, SOC2 docs, and a POC to benchmark 100k-1M vectors with rerank latency requirements.
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing options (Maya) - by 2027-03-23
Security pack (SOC2 + KMS integration guide) shared (Ravi) - by 2027-03-22
Schedule technical deep-dive to run sample benchmark with 100k vectors (Priya / Ravi) - propose 2027-03-26
Customer to provide sample dataset and target queries (Ethan) - by 2027-03-24
action_items: Maya Chen: Send estimate for Dedicated 4-GPU pod and Hosted throughput pricing (due: 2027-03-23)
Ravi Patel: Share KMS integration doc and RBAC examples (due: 2027-03-22)
Priya Sharma / Ethan Li: Share 10k sample vectors + 200 sample queries for benchmark (due: 2027-03-24)
Diana Ortega: Confirm internal stakeholders for compliance review (due: 2027-03-25)
transcript:
Header: 2027-03-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: 47 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Torres (Redwood Solutions), Diana Ortega (Head of Search, Pioneer), Priya Sharma (ML Lead), Ethan Li (Data Engineer), Samir Khan (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Diana: Hi, Diana here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya — ML.
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan — data eng.
[00:14] Samir: Samir from Product.
[00:16] Ravi: Ravi, SE on the Redwood side. Liam also on for a few minutes.
[00:22] Maya: Perfect. Aim today is to understand your current embedding / search stack and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense and outline a POC. Cool?
[00:30] Diana: Yep, that's right. We're currently running a hybrid system — keyword-based Elastic for exact matches and Pinecone for semantic. It's kinda split, costs are creeping up and latency spikes on our busiest endpoints.
[00:45] Priya: To add — our vectors are 1536-d right now using an off-the-shelf model, but we're debating moving to 768-d for cost. We're also experimenting with a cross-encoder rerank as a second-stage to improve precision on top-k.
[01:00] Maya: Nice — that maps to a lot of conversations we see. Quick question on throughput: what's your peak QPS for search and what latency SLO do you have for first-stage vs rerank?
[01:12] Ethan: Peak is about 350 QPS for search during business hours. First-stage needs sub-80ms ideally, rerank can be up to 250–300ms but we try to keep the whole user experience under 350ms.
[01:28] Samir: And for some enterprise customers we have tighter SLAs so predictability matters a lot — cost predictability too.
[01:36] Ravi: Understood. On the Redwood side we usually do a two-stage pattern: fast ANN retrieval (HNSW / IVF) to get a candidate set then optional cross-encoder / LLM rerank. We support integrations with hosted vector DBs like Pinecone and Weaviate as well as customers running Milvus on-prem. You mentioned hybrid, is the rerank step currently in your service or a separate pipeline?
[01:57] Priya: It's a separate microservice. We pull top-100 from Pinecone and call our cross-encoder which scores and reorders. It's adding ~180ms on average.
[02:06] Maya: Okay. A few things we can help with: 1) embedding generation throughput — Redwood Hosted can do high-concurrency embedding calls and Dedicated provides committed GPU pods if you want faster, cheaper per-token. 2) rerank: we can host cross-encoder models on Dedicated for low latency or you can run rerank in your stack and just use Redwood for retrieval embeddings. 3) dimensionality — sometimes lower-d embeddings (e.g., 384/768) with a good model plus rerank give same UX at lower cost.
[02:32] Diana: Curious, what's the dimensionality tradeoff in practice? We saw recall drop when moving from 1536 to 768 on a subset, but maybe our reranker was weak.
[02:42] Ravi: Right, recall vs vector size is workload dependent. We usually recommend benchmarking: for some corpora 768 is fine; for others, especially fine-grained legal/finance queries, 1536 beats. Also HNSW index parameters (efConstruction, efSearch) have big impact. Sometimes you can reduce dimensions and increase efSearch and still get good recall with lower storage/compute.
[03:02] Priya: So for the POC we'd want to test both dims and rerank tradeoffs — like top-200 first-stage at 768 + cross-encoder vs top-100 at 1536 without rerank.
[03:12] Maya: Totally. We can scope that. On integration: do you want Redwood to manage embeddings + vector store, or just embeddings and you keep Pinecone?
[03:22] Diana: Ideally we'd consolidate to reduce ops. But vendor lock-in is a concern. Also our compliance team wants KMS and audit logs for embeddings — no plaintext storage in vendor-managed unless we have envelope encryption.
[03:34] Ravi: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) addresses that — you get customer-managed KMS and audit logs, plus we can deploy control plane into your VPC. Dedicated also supports KMS and private networking options depending on contract. We have SOC2 and we can share the security pack after this call.
[03:50] Samir: Good, please share SOC2 and our legal will look.
[03:54] Maya: We'll send it — action item.
[03:57] [04:00] Ethan: One more infra question: for 350 QPS with 1536-d vectors and top-100 retrieval, what kind of Dedicated pod do you recommend?
[04:12] Ravi: Ballpark — a 4x A100-equivalent Dedicated pod for embeddings + retrieval might be safe if you want headroom and burst. But if you offload retrieval to a vector DB like Milvus or Pinecone, Dedicated primarily for embedding generation and rerank can be smaller. We'll size explicitly in the follow-up with sample queries.
[04:30] Priya: For rerank, is it better to run a cross-encoder (bi-encoder+cross) on CPU or GPU? Our current cross-encoder is CPU-bound and that's why it's 180ms.
[04:40] Ravi: Cross-encoders are compute heavy — GPU hosting reduces latency significantly. On Dedicated you can run a quantized cross-encoder on GPU for much lower latency. Also Redwood has caching between retrieval and rerank that can skip rerank if candidate order is stable.
[04:55] Maya: We should also discuss ANN choices. You're using Pinecone; are you on their default HNSW config?
[05:02] Priya: Yes, default HNSW. We haven't tuned efSearch.
[05:06] Ravi: Increasing efSearch raises recall at cost of CPU and latency. Another lever is vector dimensionality and using PQ/quantization in the vector DB. Milvus/Weaviate offer more control if you self-host.
[05:18] Diana: Our legal asked about data residency — some EU customer data needs to stay in eu-west region. Can Redwood route embeddings regionally?
[05:26] Maya: Yes, smart routing by policy is supported. We can pin requests by region and provide Private deployment options. We'll need to confirm regions for Dedicated if you pick reserved capacity.
[05:36] [06:00] Maya: Quick demo idea — we can run a 100k vector benchmark. Priya/Ethan would give sample vectors and queries, we'll run: Hosted baseline, Dedicated 4-GPU pod baseline, and Private prototype if you need KMS. Then measure first-stage latency at QPS profile and full rerank latency. Does that sound good?
[06:18] Priya: Yes. Also can we test hybrid search: vector + BM25 combined scoring?
[06:25] Ravi: Absolutely. We support hybrid search flows — combining keyword scores and vector similarity, and reranking on combined signal. Some customers do linear blend, others learn a combiner. We can instrument per-route metrics in Console to compare quality.
[06:39] Ethan: Any constraints on vector size for storage? We currently have ~1.2M vectors.
[06:44] Ravi: 1.2M is fine; storage and index rebuild times matter. We can shard indices and do rolling rebuilds. If you go to 1536 you pay more for storage, and retrieval CPU increases. Dedicated helps with predictable rebuilds.
[06:58] Diana: What's the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated roughly? We need to justify ops savings vs commitments.
[07:06] Maya: High level: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-token/per-embedding price but no infra ops. Dedicated is discounted unit price with a monthly/annual commit; you trade capex for predictability. We'll include an example TCO in the follow-up.
[07:18] Samir: Do you support HSM or customer-managed KMS?
[07:22] Ravi: Yes, customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations are supported for Private and in many Dedicated configurations. We'll include the integration guide.
[07:30] [08:00] Priya: For the reranker model, can Redwood host custom models or is it limited to Redwood-approved models?
[08:08] Ravi: You can bring-your-own-model (BYOM) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have curated models; we also support uploading containers for Private deployments. There may be vetting for very large custom models but BYOM is standard.
[08:23] Priya: Good. We have a proprietary cross-encoder that we prefer to keep in-house; so probably Dedicated or Private.
[08:29] Maya: Makes sense. For the POC, we can run a hybrid approach: you keep rerank in your environment, we run embeddings + retrieval tests; then we test migrating rerank to Dedicated GPU and measure latency delta.
[08:42] Diana: Sounds pragmatic.
[08:45] [09:00] Ethan: A few nitty-gritty questions: batch size limits for embedding calls, rate limiting behavior, and how Redwood handles KV cache for conversational contexts (even though we're doing search, some flows are conversational).
[09:14] Ravi: Embedding endpoints support batching — we can tune concurrency and batch size; larger batch sizes reduce per-embedding cost but increase tail latency. Rate limits are configurable per-account; Dedicated gives more predictable throughput. KV cache is mostly used for generative caching, but caching/prefix caching can be applied to repeated embeddings and rerank results if queries repeat.
[09:34] Priya: Do you persist raw text anywhere? Compliance is sensitive about unencrypted raw PII.
[09:40] Maya: We can avoid persisting raw inputs in Hosted by configuring no-logging or using Private where logs stay in your VPC and you control retention. We'll note that as an action item and include documentation.
[09:53] [10:00] Samir: Any customers running similar scale POC?
[10:04] Ravi: Yes, we've done 1M+ vector pilots with search companies and fintechs — common patterns: use Dedicated for embedding generation and GPU rerank, vector DB (self-hosted) for retrieval, or consolidate into Redwood-managed vector store if they want less ops.
[10:20] Maya: Okay let's outline POC success criteria — Priya, Diana, Samir, tell me what you'd measure?
[10:28] Priya: Recall@10 >= current baseline, full pipeline 95th percentile latency < 350ms, and cost per query reduced by 20% over 3 months.
[10:36] Diana: And security checks passed (SOC2 + KMS), and predictable capacity for enterprise customers.
[10:42] Samir: Also a migration plan that doesn't require 3 months of rework.
[10:46] Maya: Great — we'll put that in the follow-up.
[10:50] [11:00] Maya: Any blockers or concerns we should know about?
[11:04] Priya: Licensing for some pre-trained models is a slight concern — we'll confirm. Also we have a couple of EU-only indexes.
[11:12] Maya: Noted. We'll include model licensing guidance.
[11:16] Diana: Timeline — we want to run POC this quarter, ideally start next week. Is Redwood able to spin a test Dedicated pod quickly?
[11:24] Ravi: We can provision a Dedicated test pod within days for evaluation, subject to procurement agreements. Hosted tests can start immediately.
[11:32] Maya: Great. Final recap: Redwood will send pricing and Dedicated sizing, security docs (SOC2, KMS guide), propose slots for technical deep-dive and benchmarking, and customer will share sample dataset and confirm stakeholders.
[11:50] Priya: We'll send samples and queries by Wednesday.
[11:54] Ethan: I'll coordinate the data extraction.
[11:58] Diana: We'll review legal/compliance on the security pack.
[12:02] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and links.
[12:06] [12:00] End of call. 

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and run-on sentences; speaker labels were set by the recorder (some segments labeled generically in our system). Shared artifacts: link to Redwood Dedicated sizing template (will be attached), security pack (SOC2+KMS), example benchmark spreadsheet.
